addProblem.title: Add New Problem
addProblem.problemIdHint: Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only
addProblem.codeTemplatesHint: Provide starter code templates for each language. At least one template is required.
addProblem.solutionTemplatesHint: Optionally provide reference solutions for the problem.

aiGenerator.title: AI Problem Generator
aiGenerator.subtitle: Describe the type of coding problem you want to practice. The AI will generate a custom algorithm problem for you.
aiGenerator.requestPlaceholder: e.g., I want to do a dynamic programming problem, or I want to do a string processing problem
aiGenerator.instruction1: Describe the type of problem you want (algorithm type, difficulty, topic)
aiGenerator.instruction2: You can write in English or Chinese
aiGenerator.instruction3: Be specific about what you want to practice (e.g., "dynamic programming", "graph algorithms")
aiGenerator.instruction4: The AI will generate a complete problem with test cases and solutions
aiGenerator.instruction5: The generated problem will be automatically added to your problem collection
aiGenerator.noAIProviderConfigured: No AI provider is configured. Please configure one of the supported AI providers in your environment variables.
aiGenerator.jsonParseError: Failed to parse the generated JSON. You can fix it in the editor below.
aiGenerator.fixJsonInstructions: The AI generated content that couldn't be parsed as valid JSON. Please fix any syntax errors and save the corrected JSON.
aiGenerator.invalidJsonFormat: Invalid JSON format. Please check for syntax errors.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Configure AI model providers for problem generation, AI chat, and AI solutions

defaultProvider.title: Default AI Provider
defaultProvider.description: Select the default AI provider for all AI features (problem generation, AI chat, AI solution). You can configure multiple providers below and switch between them.
defaultProvider.label: AI Provider
defaultProvider.selectDescription: Choose which AI provider to use by default

settings.modelHint: Leave empty to use the default. Any model id works.

manage.title: Manage Problems
manage.importFromFolderDescription: Load all JSON files from a local folder. Each JSON file can contain a single problem or an array of problems.
manage.problemsFolderHint: Load all JSON files from the 'problems' folder in the application directory
manage.customFolderHint: Enter the full path to a folder containing JSON problem files
manage.importDescription: Enter one or more URLs to JSON files containing problems. Each URL should point to an array of problem objects. You can enter multiple URLs, one per line.
manage.multiUrlHint: Enter one URL per line to import from multiple sources
manage.jsonFormatDescription: JSON files should contain an array of problem objects (or a single problem object) with the following structure:
manage.deleteConfirmMessage: Are you sure you want to delete {{count}} problem(s)? This action cannot be undone.

list.title: Engineering Practice
list.entryHint: Move from puzzles to systems: a real multi-file workspace, stage-by-stage builds, reviewed on concurrency, latency, encapsulation and elegance.
list.heading: Engineering projects
list.subtitle: Each project is a small system you build in stages. You work in a full multi-file workspace, and the hidden acceptance specs check more than correctness, they gate on engineering metrics like concurrency and latency.

stage.label: Stage {{current}}/{{total}}
stage.locked: Clear the previous stage to unlock
stage.referenceLocked: Clear this stage to see the reference implementation
stage.pitfallsHint: These pass some specs but are wrong as engineering

workspace.readonlyHint: Contract file provided by the platform, read only
workspace.noFileOpen: Pick a file on the left to start
workspace.editedHint: This file differs from the stage starter. Click to see the diff. Your edits are saved automatically.
workspace.languageHint: Switching swaps the starter files and specs; each language keeps its own drafts

metrics.timelineHint: Virtual time on the x-axis, in-flight requests on the y-axis, a sequential implementation is a flat line at 1.

score.scaledByPassRate: Engineering score scaled by the acceptance pass rate ({percent}%): how fast it runs is not credit while it is wrong
score.notMeasured: Nothing to measure in this run

review.title: AI engineering review
review.subtitle: Reviewed like a pull request: concurrency safety, failure behaviour, module boundaries, abstractions
review.empty: Ask AI to review the workspace the way a staff engineer would. It sees your code, the latest run and the static analysis metrics.

chat.title: Engineering assistant
chat.empty: I can see your workspace code, the stage goal and your latest run. Ask about approach, failures or design trade-offs.
chat.placeholder: Ask about the current implementation… (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a newline)

prompts.metrics: Why are my concurrency/latency gates failing?
prompts.howToStart: Where should I start this stage?
prompts.design: What design options do I have?

generator.title: Generate a project
generator.heading: Generate an engineering project
generator.subtitle: Describe the engineering skill you want to drill. AI designs a staged, multi-file project with hidden specs, metric gates and a reference solution.
generator.requestLabel: What do you want to practise
generator.requestHint: Be specific: the kind of system, and the engineering concern you want tested (concurrency, caching, resilience, boundaries…)
generator.placeholder: e.g. a log batching uploader with backpressure, batching and drop policy
generator.verifyNote: The platform runs the reference solution to verify the generated project before saving it
generator.loadingHint: Generating and verifying: design stages → write specs → execute the reference solution → repair. This usually takes 1-3 minutes.
generator.problemsTitle: Problems found while executing this project
generator.noDiscrimination: the starter skeleton also passes, specs lack discrimination
generator.repairing: Verification failed, asking for a fix…

cloud.disabledBody: You turned cloud features off in Settings. Problems, engineering practice and the workshop are unaffected; turn it back on to reach the market and your account.
cloud.notConfiguredTitle: This deployment has no cloud configured
cloud.notConfiguredBody: The server answered but has no database, so accounts and the market are unavailable. For a self-hosted deployment, set DATABASE_URL and AUTH_SECRET as described in the cloud deployment guide.
cloud.offlineBody: Either this machine is offline or the server is down. Your local problems, practice history and workshop drafts are unaffected.
cloud.settingsDescription: Accounts and the problem market. With this off the client makes no cloud requests at all, and everything else keeps working.
cloud.enableHint: When off, the market and account entries are hidden and no network probe is made
cloud.baseHint: Point this at your own backend, or leave it empty to use the official deployment

account.title: Account
account.passwordChangeSignsOutOthers: Changing the password signs out your other devices
account.optionalHint: An account is only used for the problem market. Everything local works without one.
account.noListings: Nothing published yet. Write a problem in the workshop, then publish it.

market.title: Problem market
market.subtitle: Browse and download algorithm problems and engineering projects written by other people, and publish your own.
market.starSignInHint: Sign in to star and publish problems.
market.installed: Installed into your local library as {{id}}
market.readOnlyLibrary: This deployment has a read-only library. Use the desktop app or a local server, or export the JSON instead.
market.executionNotice: A downloaded problem carries its own test cases and reference solution, and running it executes that code on your machine — in the same WASM sandbox and Web Worker your own code runs in.

workshop.title: Workshop
workshop.subtitle: Write, verify and publish your own problems. Drafts stay in this browser and work offline.
workshop.forkHint: Copy an existing problem as a starting point. The id gets a -copy suffix.
workshop.forkNotFound: That problem is not in the library
workshop.noDrafts: No drafts yet. Create one, or fork something from your library.
workshop.confirmDelete: Delete the draft "{{title}}"? This cannot be undone.
workshop.offlineNotice: The workshop works entirely offline: drafts live in this browser, the AI assistant uses the provider you configured (Ollama runs locally), and verification runs on your machine. Only publishing needs the network and an account.
workshop.draftMissingBody: It was either deleted, or it lives in another browser or on another machine.
workshop.verifyNeedsSolution: Write a reference solution first — without one there is no way to check the test cases.
workshop.verifyPassed: The reference solution passes all {{total}} cases ({{passed}}/{{total}}).
workshop.verifyStagesPassed: All {{count}} stages pass, and none of the starter skeletons do — the specs discriminate.
workshop.savedToLibrary: Saved to your local library as {{id}}
workshop.publishNew: This problem has not been published. Publishing puts it in the market.
workshop.publishUpdate: Update the published "{{slug}}". The version number goes up by one.
workshop.publishUnverified: Verification has not passed yet. Run it before publishing — the first thing anyone does after downloading is run it.
workshop.changelogHint: Optional, shown in the version history
workshop.aiTemplatesHint: Empty templates in five languages, matching the reference solution's signature
workshop.aiDraftStage: Have AI draft the next stage
workshop.aiDraftStageHint: Say what the stage should exercise, or leave it empty to continue the difficulty curve
workshop.testsAdded: Added {{count}} test cases. Check every expected output yourself.
workshop.templateHint: What the reader sees when they open the problem. No solution in here.
workshop.solutionHint: Used to verify the test cases, and shown after the problem is solved
workshop.testsHint: input is the argument list, output is the JSON-encoded return value
workshop.sharedFilesHint: Files every stage shares, usually the read-only interface contract
workshop.starterFilesHint: Added to the workspace when the stage begins. They should fail this stage's specs.
workshop.specsHint: Invisible to the reader, injected into the workspace when acceptance runs
workshop.referenceFilesHint: Every path here needs a matching starter file
workshop.gatesHint: Assertions on measured metrics, for example peak concurrency at most 4
workshop.labConfigHint: Network simulation: default latency, concurrency ceiling, failure rate, per-endpoint overrides
